title: SYSK Selects: How Bullfighting Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the 2011-era episode "How Bullfighting Works," reintroduced by Chuck, who says he chose it because he opposes bullfighting. The hosts cover the history of bullfighting from ancient bull rituals and the Iberian Peninsula through the Visigoths, mounted bullfighting in Portugal, the San Fermin festival and running of the bulls, royal and aristocratic patronage, and bans by Isabella and Philip. They walk through a corrida: the treatment of bulls before the ring, the three tercios, picador, banderillero and matador roles, the estocada and descabello, the indulto, and the abuse of horses. They discuss famous matadors (Juan Belmonte, Joselito, Manolete), bull breeding, declining attendance and the Catalonia ban, Spanish TV restrictions, government subsidies, and the bulldog and bear-baiting comparisons. The episode closes with listener mail about comics history and design contests.

segments.title: Selects intro and host's stance
segments.summary: Chuck introduces this Selects rerun of the bullfighting episode and says he opposes bullfighting and is republishing it to encourage people to stop it.

segments.title: Hosts' experiences and bullfighting statistics
segments.summary: The hosts discuss attending bullfights, tourists attending and booing, the number of bulls killed each year, and matador deaths, including Julio Aparicio being gored.

segments.title: Ancient origins and Visigoth influence
segments.summary: The hosts trace bull rituals to ancient times, including Mycenaean bull leaping, and describe Visigoth-era mounted bullfighting that led to horseback bullfighting in Portugal.

segments.title: Festivals, running of the bulls and royal bans
segments.summary: Bullfighting became established in Spain by the eleventh century during festivals, linked to San Fermin in Pamplona and the running of the bulls. Royal and aristocratic patronage followed, with Queen Isabella and Pope Pius V opposing it and Philip II banning it among the nobility.

segments.title: Bull treatment before the fight
segments.summary: The hosts describe how bulls are treated in the days before the fight, including sleep deprivation, blinding, drugs, laxatives, confinement in a dark box, and transport.

segments.title: Structure of a corrida: tercios and picadors
segments.summary: The fight is divided into three tercios. In the first, picadors on horseback lance the bull's neck to weaken its muscles. The hosts also explain the role of the cape and that bulls are not angered by red.

segments.title: Banderilleros, matador and the kill
segments.summary: Banderilleros place barbed darts in the bull. The matador has a set time to kill with a sword, and the estocada and descabello are described. The hosts describe a bull sometimes surviving and being dragged out, and the crowd's reactions.

segments.title: Indulto, horses, and famous matadors
segments.summary: The indulto reprieve for brave bulls is described, with the bull Manzanito as an example. The hosts also cover horse abuse, including stuffed ears and severed vocal cords, and then famous matadors Juan Belmonte, Joselito, and Manolete.

segments.title: Bull breeding, matador pay and bull testing
segments.summary: Fighting bulls are about four years old and weigh about 1,300 pounds, bred and tested for bravery. The hosts discuss matador pay and the claim that bulls are altered to be easier to fight, and make an off-topic Rocky III digression.

segments.title: Decline, bans and suffering
segments.summary: The hosts discuss declining attendance, the Catalonia ban effective January 2012, the 2010 poll, Spanish TV restrictions, government subsidies sustaining events, a vet's study on bull suffering, and the debate over animal suffering versus pain. They also cover bear baiting and bulldog history and the call to contact embassies.

segments.title: Closing opinions
segments.summary: The hosts give their closing opinions against bullfighting, calling it outdated and cruel, and say culture should bring people together.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts read listener mail about a comics history episode from an illustrator and discuss a T-shirt design contest, then give social media and email contact information.
